templates.pattern: Light travels from air into a medium at a speed of [V] × 10⁶ m/s. What is the refractive index of the medium? (c = 3 × 10⁸ m/s)
Light travels from air into a medium of refractive index [N]. The angle of incidence is [AI] degrees. What is the sine of the angle of refraction? (sin 30°=0.500, sin 45°=0.707, sin 60°=0.866)
templates.explanation: Snell's law: n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂. With n₁=1 (air): sin θ₂ = sin [AI]° ÷ [N] = [RESULT]

templates.pattern: A glass block has refractive index [N]. What is the sine of the critical angle?
templates.explanation: sin C = 1 ÷ n = 1 ÷ [N] = [RESULT]. The critical angle is the minimum angle of incidence at which total internal reflection occurs.

templates.pattern: An image is formed [V] cm from a lens and the object is [U] cm from the lens. What is the magnification produced?
templates.explanation: Magnification = image distance ÷ object distance = [V] ÷ [U] = [RESULT]. A value greater than 1 means the image is larger than the object.

templates.pattern: A pump with [EFF]% efficiency raises [M] kg of water to a height of [H] m in [T] seconds. What is the electrical power input to the pump? (g = 10 m/s²)
templates.explanation: Useful power = mgh ÷ t = [M]×10×[H] ÷ [T] W. Input power = useful power × 100 ÷ efficiency = [M*10*H*100] ÷ ([T*EFF]) = [RESULT] W

templates.pattern: A converging lens of focal length [F] cm produces an image [V] cm from the lens. What is the object distance in cm?
templates.explanation: Lens formula rearranged: u = vF ÷ (v−F) = [V]×[F] ÷ ([V]−[F]) = [V*F] ÷ [V-F] = [RESULT] cm

templates.pattern: An object [H] cm tall is magnified [M] times by a lens. What is the height of the image in cm?
templates.explanation: Image height = object height × magnification = [H] × [M] = [RESULT] cm

templates.pattern: Light travels from medium 1 (refractive index [N1]) into medium 2 (refractive index [N2]). What is the speed of light in medium 2 in m/s? (c = 3 × 10⁸ m/s)
templates.explanation: Speed of light in medium 2 = c ÷ n₂ = 3×10⁸ ÷ [N2] = [RESULT] m/s. Since n₂ < n₁, light speeds up entering medium 2.

templates.pattern: A lens has a power of [P] dioptres. What is its focal length in cm?
templates.explanation: Power (dioptres) = 1 ÷ focal length (metres). Focal length = 1 ÷ [P] m = 100 ÷ [P] cm = [RESULT] cm
